scenes.setting: Winding down the fog session: the smurf is christened 'The World' — beginning and end of the tarot cycle — then back to the bedroom with plans to quiz Justice about the Pound family through it
scenes.text_anchor: Klein had named his smurf “The World”

scenes.setting: A dreamless night, then another day combing Backlund's public libraries for nobility records — quietly, no librarians asked this time
scenes.text_anchor: heading to the rest of the public libraries in Backlund

scenes.setting: Twenty minutes early above the gray fog: rehearsing The World, fitting the All-Black Eye to a silver chain under his sleeve
scenes.text_anchor: he sat down at the seat belonging to The Fool

scenes.setting: Tarot Club with a stranger at the table: 'a new member, Mr. World' -- Audrey reads what she can of him through the fog while the members trade greetings, and Mr. Fool sets the candidates' examination
scenes.text_anchor: “This is a new member, Mr. World.”

scenes.setting: Klein places the colored oil painting on the table -- neat black hair, round glasses, taunting brown eyes, 'formerly known alias: Lanevus' -- as Justice's task; The World asks about issuing missions, and Alger hands over six more diary pages
scenes.text_anchor: “Investigate the man in the painting. He’s in Backlund.”

scenes.setting: Diary-reading interlude: Roselle's three children — Bernadette free, Ciel bound, baby Bornova born an Astromancer; Zaratul's grim divinations of each; and Floren of the Sauron family demanding Roselle's servitude
scenes.text_anchor: “9th February. I have a third child. I named him Bornova.

scenes.setting: Diary-reading interlude continues: the two-thousand-year Sauron colossus and arrogant Floren; the ancient doomsday organization with its twenty-two paths of the divine; and Roselle's Cards of Blasphemy — anti-divination insurance hiding the ultimate secret, up to Sequence 0, the Sequence of a True God
scenes.text_anchor: “I will hide the ultimate secret of the twenty-two paths of the divine in these different Cards of Blasphemy

scenes.setting: Diary interlude's last beat: Sequence 0 — a True God above Sequence 1 in each of the twenty-two paths — leaves The Fool struggling to keep his composure before he finally lets Roselle's pages vanish
scenes.text_anchor: There's still a Sequence 0 above Sequence 1?

scenes.setting: Gathering resumes: Justice settles the Bakerland account (5000 pounds of Qilangos bounty still owed); Mr. World requests Magician ingredients plus the Apothecary's marrow crystals — Derrick offers Mist Treant parts for a weapon, Audrey wants the Psychiatrist formula, Alger the Wind-blessed
scenes.text_anchor: “Miss Justice, well done. You finished Bakerland in less than a week.

scenes.setting: The World commissions a census of Loen's abject nobles from Justice, paying in a private lesson on the Demoness Sect's Witch and Pleasure Sequences (to Audrey's scandalized fascination), then buys the Sauron-family answer from Mr. Fool for a Sequence 7 formula
scenes.text_anchor: “I want to get information about all the abject nobles in the Loen Kingdom

scenes.setting: Members gone: a satisfied puppeteer lets The World bow and melt back into the palace, stores the All-Black Eye behind the bronze table, and descends drained
scenes.text_anchor: With a smurf, a lot of things are really much more convenient.

scenes.setting: Rare Backlund sunshine behind the curtains: a half-hour nap, then a daylight carriage toward the outskirts — tonight, the cemetery test of Azik's copper whistle
scenes.text_anchor: Klein was going to test the influence of Azik's copper whistle

scenes.setting: Aston Cemetery after dark: whistle experiment one — corpses laid to rest by priestly ritual, old grave and fresh grave alike, ignore Azik's copper whistle entirely
scenes.text_anchor: “Friend, if you are passing by, help me up. Thanks!”

scenes.setting: St. Estin's Hospital morgue in the small hours: unshielded for two minutes, the whistle sits a corpse upright and sets the cabinets banging — three Requiem Charms quiet the dead, and Klein ceiling-perches past the investigating janitor and strolls home content
scenes.text_anchor: At that moment, a corpse on a long table suddenly sat up!

scenes.setting: An empty horse track outside Empress Borough: valiant riding-clothes Audrey hands Xio and Fors a satchel of Lanevus wanted portraits (with her own disguise-variant sketches) for 100 pounds; Fors has a lead on the Psychology Alchemists through a new gathering
scenes.text_anchor: “Formerly used name: Lanevus, wanted swindler.”

scenes.setting: Late Tuesday start: a note on the door ('Owner is out...') to keep Millet Carter believing his fifty pounds are hard at work, then off to a planned day of leisure
scenes.text_anchor: “Owner is out and will be back after five in the afternoon.”

scenes.setting: Quelaag Club: Talim Dumont drops the Gale divorce news with a knowing smile — then sounds Klein out about marksmanship and fighting for a troubled friend
scenes.text_anchor: “Good morning. Mary and Doragu are getting a divorce.”

scenes.setting: The club's underground range: near-perfect revolver groupings, then trainee-knight Talim flipped flat on his back in one exchange — the friend needing protection is Daily Observer reporter Mike Joseph
scenes.text_anchor: Holding onto a revolver that he rented from the Quelaag Club

scenes.setting: Over cream cheese lobster: Mike's serial-killer scoop — eleven women dead, all former street girls except sixteen-year-old Siber of the Golden Rose; he hires Klein as escort for his brothel visit, one pound quiet or five with a fight
scenes.text_anchor: “11! Another lady killed! Sivellaus Yard is helpless!”

scenes.setting: The Golden Rose, 19 Hope Street: Backlund's 'best legal brothel' by daylight; Mike dances with a girl Siber's age — she knew the victim, but Ma'am Lopez has terrorized the girls into silence
scenes.text_anchor: “That's the Golden Rose, the best legal brothel

scenes.setting: Lopez lies through her orphan story (Spirit Vision says so); two bouncers dropped in silence buys one overheard line — 'Tell Capim not to send anyone over in the next few days!' — before a lock-breaking exit and a five-pound payday
scenes.text_anchor: “Tell Capim not to send anyone over in the next few days!

scenes.setting: On the street outside, the white-templed 'customer' from the hall steps from a carriage: 'Hello, I'm Detective Isengard Stanton. I'm assisting the police in this case. Can we have a chat?'
scenes.text_anchor: “Hello, I'm Detective Isengard Stanton.

scenes.setting: In Isengard Stanton's carriage: two pounds buys the overheard Capim line — the famous detective knows him at once as Cherwood's girl-trafficking magnate no evidence can touch
scenes.text_anchor: “I'm asking you on behalf of Sivellaus Yard.

scenes.setting: After Moriarty leaves, Isengard strokes a brass open-book ornament with a vertical eye and dissects the mismatch of gold-rimmed glasses and a barbaric beard for his assistant
scenes.text_anchor: The brass ornament was a pocket-sized open book with a vertical eye in the center.

scenes.setting: On the tracked public carriage: Spirit Vision showed Isengard locked in pure rational blue and spirituality purple — observation genius, or Beyonder?
scenes.text_anchor: That Detective Isengard Stanton is problematic.

scenes.setting: Bravehearts Bar: Maric hasn't shown for two days and hidden gazes track his name — someone is hunting him; Klein aborts the visit with a card-game excuse, guessing Miss Bodyguard and Maric are both fugitives from something with real teeth
scenes.text_anchor: “He didn't come. He didn't come yesterday either.”

scenes.setting: Counter-surveillance via the East Borough bolt-hole, then home to the mailbox: the Ernst Firm ad is in the Morning Post — gathering tomorrow at eight, and formulas to sell
scenes.text_anchor: It was an advertisement for the Ernst Firm's purchase of goods!

scenes.setting: Getting there in disguise as a bearded workman, worrying the whole way that Eye of Wisdom will see through it, until the door creaks open and the attendant hands over a hooded black robe
scenes.text_anchor: It would be best if Eye of Wisdom and the Apothecary don’t recognize me.

scenes.setting: Inside at last: one candle, hooded members all round, and Klein sells the Bard and Light Suppliant formulas for 600 pounds to the chubby Apothecary — notarized genuine by Eye of Wisdom's ring
scenes.text_anchor: There was only one candle in the dark and silent room

scenes.setting: The auction: Klein outbids for the Axe of Hurricane at 560 pounds (its 50% storm-lightning proc is made for the City of Silver), a Corpse Collector formula sells fast, nobody has Dark Patterned Black Panther spinal fluid, and the Apothecary admits he never checked whether the sewer beast was dealt with
scenes.text_anchor: “The second weapon is called the Axe of Hurricane.

scenes.setting: The lightless Black Palm Street apartment, then above the fog: the axe carried up whole — 'The World has sacrificed the weapon to me. You can prepare the bestowment ritual.'
scenes.text_anchor: he summoned himself and carried the Axe of Hurricane above the gray fog

scenes.setting: City of Silver: Derrick practices sword slashes imagining his new blade — straight sword, broadsword, rapier? The ritual delivers... an axe
scenes.text_anchor: It was an axe.

scenes.setting: Above the fog: The Sun's grateful reply — he'll gather the Mist Treant's true root and juice as soon as he can; Klein relays the axe's quirks and descends
scenes.text_anchor: “Dear Mr. Fool, please tell Mr. World that I'll try to gather the Mist Treant's true root

scenes.setting: A cramped Dharavi Street pub: Xio recruits informant Williams onto the Lanevus hunt (five soli now, ten pounds for a hit), fails to reform his Half-and-Half habits, and quells a brawl with one Arbiter shout
scenes.text_anchor: “Williams, I have something to talk to you about.”

scenes.setting: St. George Borough, Thursday: Leppard's crude bicycle prototype rides well; second payment promised next week — and the inventor insists on calling it a 'bike'
scenes.text_anchor: Leppard was progressing very quickly on the bicycle project

scenes.setting: Home at noon amid illusory prayers: Julianne formally delivers Mrs. Sammer's Sunday-luncheon invitation; Klein eyes his messy rooms and plots to borrow her cleaning services
scenes.text_anchor: “Mr. Moriarty, Mrs. Sammer would like to invite you to a Sunday luncheon.

scenes.setting: Above the gray fog: Justice sacrifices her abject-nobles manuscript through the illusory door; Klein reads the Pound chapter — two heirs 'dead of illness' thirty-two years ago, and Baronet Pound now at 29 Sivellaus Street, Empress Borough
scenes.text_anchor: “… I've gathered the information regarding the abject nobles.

scenes.setting: 29 Sivellaus Street, across from the Yard itself: a clown-painted intruder quizzes drunken Baronet Rafter Pound — faceless servants who searched the house for years — then Slumber-Charms him for dream-walking and spirit channeling; all answers ring true
scenes.text_anchor: His face was painted red, yellow, and white, looking like the funniest clown!

scenes.setting: After the window clicks shut, Rafter Pound's eyes snap open — ringed with ruptured capillaries — and fix on the open oriel window
scenes.text_anchor: Around those light blue eyes, there was a circle of ruptured capillaries!

scenes.setting: Above the gray fog with Rafter's stolen hairs: sidestepping the six gods' entanglement, Klein divines 'Rafter Pound's future' to confirm the past
scenes.text_anchor: “Rafter Pound's future.”

scenes.setting: Above the gray fog (visions only: a future Rafter Pound crawling from a cave wearing the Tudor scepter emblem): the fourth test unmasks the baronet as a probable Tudor descendant playing broken — Klein resolves to just dynamite the ruins shut and stay out of it
scenes.text_anchor: “Tudor!” Klein jerked out of the dream and sat up.

scenes.setting: Quelaag Club at tea time: Mike confirms Siber died to a copycat, not the serial killer, and brokers Mary a pollution-council interview — the club doing what private clubs do best
scenes.text_anchor: “I've roughly figured out who Capim is.

scenes.setting: Williams's East Borough room at dusk: a towering hooded shadow asks who wants Lanevus, gets Xio Derecha's name, pats him goodbye — then a snap of fingers shreds him, and a rigged gas candle erases the evidence
scenes.text_anchor: “Who told you to look for Lanevus?”

scenes.setting: The Bravehearts billiard room: Klein asks Kaspars for mining explosives and a demolition expert — after swearing it's a private secret-chamber demolition, not a bank job
scenes.text_anchor: “I want to buy explosives, the kind that is widely used in mines.”

scenes.setting: Miss Bodyguard materializes — 'Ma'am. Sharron', Kaspars names her at last: Maric is gone for good, she IS a demolition expert, and she'll seal the ruins free of charge so only she can pass through; zombies borrowed as 'snake-repelling assistants'
scenes.text_anchor: “Good evening, Ma'am. Sharron.”

scenes.setting: Saturday morning: the Backlund Bulletin reports the Dharavi Street gas explosion — Williams dead without a complete corpse; grieving Xio vows vengeance and turns back to move house before hunting the killer's trail
scenes.text_anchor: 1 Dharavi Street… Apartment #03-06… Isn't this… Isn't this the place Williams rents?

scenes.setting: 10:14 at 8 Williams Street: the detective returns in worker's garb with three taciturn 'snake-repelling experts' — Maric's zombies — while the invisible Sharron surveys the terrain for the blast
scenes.text_anchor: “Yes, they're very good at repelling snakes.”

scenes.setting: The Fourth Epoch hall goes dark for good: Sharron rigs the charges with wordless professionalism (and lights the fuse 'in passing'), the blast seals the entrance under boulders, and Azik's whistle stays calm — the evil spirit remains bound
scenes.text_anchor: Sharron finished setting up the explosives and, in passing, lit the fuse.

scenes.setting: Back in the basement: the 'it just collapsed' story lands perfectly; Millet Carter pays the balance partly in gold coins from his watch-chain box, and the three zombies stroll off unescorted
scenes.text_anchor: “That underground structure is too old, it hasn't been repaired in a long time.

scenes.setting: Evening stroll home: a police dog smells the day's gunpowder — Klein hands over his revolver with an 'I found it and was turning it in' smile and demands Lawyer Jurgen Cooper be present for any body search
scenes.text_anchor: the police dog suddenly growled at him and barked endlessly

scenes.setting: An East Borough corner: disguised-as-a-boy Xio grills drunken Zeon — Gavin, another Lanevus-hunter, 'drowned' in the Tussock after canvassing the Workers Alliance Tavern at East Balam Dock; the killer's pattern is a lunatic's
scenes.text_anchor: “Gavin! Gavin was found to have drowned in the Tussock River this morning!

scenes.setting: Rice Police Station again: Jurgen springs the 'good citizen who handed in a found revolver' free without a search — two pounds now, one pound a visit under their new formal partnership
scenes.text_anchor: “You can leave after signing your name,”

scenes.setting: Above the gray fog: Justice reports the killings around the Lanevus search; divination points to the Dharavi Street crime scene — where the killer likely still watches — and Klein resolves to hunt him using Rosago's All-Black Eye threads
scenes.text_anchor: “Honorable Mr. Fool, there's been a problem with the investigation of Lanevus…”

scenes.setting: Bearded and unrecognizable before the mirror: 'Captain, this is the first step to avenging both you and me' — and the reflection grins back
scenes.text_anchor: “Captain, this is the first step to avenging both you and me.”

scenes.setting: An abandoned medical-school classroom of skeletons and glass coffins: surgical-masked Audrey and Fors join a silent white-coated gathering — until the black-robed corpse floating in the central pillar opens its eyes: 'Let's begin.'
scenes.text_anchor: the floating black-clothed male corpse inside the upright glass pillar at the front of the classroom suddenly opened his eyes

scenes.setting: Dharavi Street at night: burning himself on the All-Black Eye in short touches, Klein sweeps the buildings — and finds the watcher INSIDE the blasted crime-scene room: a near-two-meter man fused into the shadows with beast-cold eyes; a bathroom-window exit gets him clear
scenes.text_anchor: There's someone in the destroyed room!

scenes.setting: Above the gray fog from the East Borough bolt-hole: the shadow-man's conjured portrait goes to Miss Justice with three words of authority — 'This is a clue.'
scenes.text_anchor: “This is a clue.”

scenes.setting: Leaving the corpse-professor's gathering: Mr. Fool's colored vision of the wolf-faced priest-robed man reaches Audrey (visions only: the tall suspect); in the carriage she plays the patient Spectator and arranges the clue's handoff to Xio
scenes.text_anchor: Accompanying Mr. Fool's solemn voice were scenes that looked like a film reel

scenes.setting: Dawn in the yellow fog: Klein watches a starving vagabond eat a gutter apple core — and turns 'reporter' to buy him a hot meal, hear how a worker becomes a ghost of East Borough, and leave him copper pennies and fifteen minutes of warm sleep
scenes.text_anchor: “I haven't eaten in almost three days.”

scenes.setting: The Sammers' Sunday luncheon, ten guests and three bottles from Luke's cabinet: Stelyn tallies the cost aloud and prescribes the 430-pound life
scenes.text_anchor: “It cost a total of 4 pounds and 8 soli.

scenes.setting: Workers Alliance Tavern, East Balam Dock: bearded, boot-heightened Xio nurses a rye beer watching for the portrait's face — and the door opens on a patron nearly two meters tall
scenes.text_anchor: The patron who entered was nearly two meters tall!

scenes.setting: Inside the Workers Alliance Tavern: Xio keeps chewing as the pale-haired 'Giant' — Williams's killer — orders lunch at the bar; she finishes, pays, and slips out without a backward glance
scenes.text_anchor: It's him! It's the suspected murderer!

scenes.setting: A secluded corner with dock technician Burton: the Giant has haunted the tavern for two-three months, no name, no friends — but he's been seen at the East Balam Dock Union
scenes.text_anchor: “We have given him a nickname, ‘Giant.'”

scenes.setting: Vagabond-disguised stakeout of the Dock Union: among the lunch crowd, a bronze-skinned man wipes fogged gold-rimmed glasses — those taunting eyes and mouth — Lanevus?
scenes.text_anchor: Lanevus? Xio jerked her head back, not daring to look again.

scenes.setting: The Sammers' activity room: Texas hold'em and rumors; Jurgen finds the topics 'very interesting' behind an unmoved face — then illusory pleas summon Klein to the bathroom
scenes.text_anchor: “No, their topics are very interesting.” Jurgen nodded seriously.

scenes.setting: Above the fog from the Sammers' bathroom: Justice reports the Giant and a suspected Lanevus at the Dock Union; every divination about going there fails — Lanevus may hold a True Creator shield — so Klein plans a reporter's visit with borrowed fake credentials
scenes.text_anchor: “After tailing the Giant and figuring his in and outs, they discovered a person suspected to be Lanevus

scenes.setting: The Dock Union as 'Reporter Statham': shepherded office to office by publicity man Rand until a bronze-skinned clerk with gold-rimmed glasses radiates the True Creator's aura — Klein excuses himself to a bathroom stall and weeps with silent, shaking laughter: Lanevus, found
scenes.text_anchor: That was the aura of the True Creator!

scenes.setting: Outside under early-evening clouds: organizing fake interview notes, Klein clocks Miss Xio among the vagabonds across the street and walks on without a flicker
scenes.text_anchor: Miss Xio? Klein instantly made a guess with what he knew.

scenes.setting: A carriage halts: Isengard Stanton again, now investigating Siber's copycat killing near East Balam Dock — pleasantries traded, no recognition shown
scenes.text_anchor: “I'm here to investigate a case. The death of Siber has been eliminated

scenes.setting: Above the gray fog from a club lounge (visions only: Lanevus's taunting face in the dream): divination seals it, and the answer goes to Justice — 'That is Lanevus. Tell the Church of the Evernight Goddess he has the godhood of the Fallen Creator.'
scenes.text_anchor: “That is Lanevus.

scenes.setting: At the hound training with her father and Susie, Audrey freezes: the 'simple mission' involves the True Creator's godhood — as expected of Mr. Fool
scenes.text_anchor: Audrey, who was watching her father train the hunting hounds with Susie, froze

scenes.setting: An old church corner: Susie delivers Audrey's note — 'he IS Lanevus, and he carries the True Creator's godhood; notify the Church of the Evernight Goddess' — leaving Xio whispering that she is still too weak to avenge Williams herself
scenes.text_anchor: “Godhood? The True Creator's godhood?”

scenes.setting: Masks bought at the grocery market, and at midnight the climb up the East Balam Dock clock tower: from the shadows above the great clock face, Klein dons a happy clown mask to watch Lanevus pay
scenes.text_anchor: It was a clown with the corner of its mouth sharply raised and a painted red nose.

scenes.setting: Two hours of waiting rewarded: a silent, black-painted military airship glides in like a vulture and hovers ten meters up — aerial overwatch for the hunt below
scenes.text_anchor: It was a huge airship covered in dark black paint!

scenes.setting: The raid: Red Glove Crestet Cesimir walks into a mirror world via Sealed Artifact 1-63, executes the flesh-bombing Giant, drops three Aurora Order shadows — then Lanevus descends the stairs, tears open his shirt to a flesh-woven hanged man, and declares 'Now, I'm even more of the True Creator!' as reality shatters
scenes.text_anchor: “Now, I'm even more of the True Creator!”

scenes.setting: On the clock tower: every gas lamp dies as an evil god's gaze erupts from the red-brick building, then profound darkness snuffs it out; divination says Lanevus is stripped of the godhood and fleeing by sewer — Klein free-climbs down the tower to intercept
scenes.text_anchor: “Lanevus's escape route.”

scenes.setting: Inside the wrecked building: a bleeding, kneeling Cesimir listens to Lanevus's gloating confession — the True Creator's 'sapling', the engineered rescue, every murder a signal flare — before the swindler yanks out the holy bone sword, fails to kill anyone, and dives for the sewers
scenes.text_anchor: “Goodbye, foolish Nighthawks.

scenes.setting: Deep in the sewer maze, Lanevus runs into a card buried in his chest — thrown by a medium-sized man in a worker's uniform wearing a happy clown mask
scenes.text_anchor: It was a happy clown.

scenes.setting: The sewer death battle: tarot cards as daggers, acrobatic dodging, the double-edged Slumber Charm gambit — Klein wakes first, crushes the throat, blinds both eyes, snaps the neck, and kicks the head from the corpse. 'Why… do you… want to… kill me…' — 'No reason.' The clown mask laughs until it weeps: 'Captain… look, we've saved Loen once again' — and the Clown potion digests completely
scenes.text_anchor: “Why… do you… want to… kill me…”

scenes.setting: No time to retrieve the scattered cards before the Nighthawks arrive — so Klein turns the problem into theater: an eye-sized badge pocketed from the corpse, and the whole tarot deck rained over headless Lanevus like a ritual sacrifice
scenes.text_anchor: allowing the tarot cards to fall, like leaves cascading over the headless corpse

scenes.setting: Two minutes later: Cesimir's exhausted team finds The Emperor and Wheel of Fortune in Lanevus's eyes, Death and The Hermit across the corpse — a scene so symbolic the Beyonders stand dazed in the dark
scenes.text_anchor: There were two tarot cards stuck in his head. One was The Emperor and the other was Wheel of Fortune.

scenes.setting: Black Palm Street cleanup: everything incriminating stashed above the fog (including Lanevus's badge — 'You can join if you have this item'); revenge done, Klein's mind settles into calm plans for Magician and the detective life
scenes.text_anchor: “You can join if you have this item.”

scenes.setting: At dawn, 'doctors' with an infectious-disease story dose every dormitory resident — each vomits a putrid blood-blob into iron barrels: the True Creator's flesh bombs quietly harvested
scenes.text_anchor: “We've discovered an infectious disease in this building.

scenes.setting: Count Hall's villa, early: Glaint relays Kance's gossip — the Aurora Order's great ploy foiled, Lanevus dead under a blanket of tarot cards; Audrey realizes at once whose signature that is
scenes.text_anchor: Tarot cards? The body was covered with tarot cards?

scenes.setting: Audrey pictures the tarot-strewn corpse — a tussle at the level of deities won by a 'simple mission' — while Glaint gushes about the style and Susie shifts guiltily at 'only a dog'
scenes.text_anchor: It's our Tarot Club! Audrey answered silently

scenes.setting: Beneath Saint Samuel Cathedral: Daly rages at being left out of the Lanevus op; the investigation pins the killer as a card-throwing Clown of the 'Secret Order'; Cesimir orders vigilance against Aurora Order reprisals and flags East Borough as an evil-god hotbed for the Council of Cardinals
scenes.text_anchor: “Why wasn't I informed of this matter?

scenes.setting: A slept-in morning, groceries, and rare afternoon sun: the avenged detective lazes in his splendid mood until a quarter to three
scenes.text_anchor: Klein slept in and didn't wake up until it was late.

scenes.setting: The Tarot Club convenes: Justice probes with a pointed 'simple mission completed' — and Mr. Fool sighs about East Borough's hotbeds for an evil god's descent, to Alger's bafflement
scenes.text_anchor: “The ‘simple' mission you entrusted has been completed.”

scenes.setting: The 'simple mission' shows its real weight: Alger suspects a silent contest between deities and forces himself not to ask, while Audrey reads Mr. Fool's sigh and understands the whole of it — the godhood Lanevus carried was the foundation for the True Creator's descent on Backlund
scenes.text_anchor: So it turns out that the bit of godhood that Lanevus possessed

scenes.setting: The World recites East Borough's brutal arithmetic — no grandfathers who aren't from the countryside, no third generation, workers withered by thirty — and Audrey, her world overturned, resolves to steer the kingdom's policy through her father
scenes.text_anchor: “any person who's a grandfather must be from the countryside.

scenes.setting: Diary-reading interlude, the final promised page: unsealed High-Sequence objects intermittently attract same-pathway Beyonders (is the gray fog itself the attractor?); a Demoness dalliance; and the second Card of Blasphemy hidden as a bookmark in 'a very valuable book'
scenes.text_anchor: “20th January. I finished making the second Card of Blasphemy.

scenes.setting: Trading resumes: Derrick raves about the axe and promises the Mist Treant parts soon; Alger dangles a grand pirate gathering on the Sonia Sea where the Panther spinal fluid or Elf-spring crystals may surface — for the right price
scenes.text_anchor: “There will be a grand event held on the Sonia Sea soon.

scenes.setting: Seller and notary in one: The World offers the incomplete Unshadowed formula, Alger shockingly declines — so The Fool 'arbitrates' a secrets-for-ingredients swap, selling Alger the Sequence 0 revelation for the Panther spinal fluid and Elf-spring crystals; Audrey and Derrick sketch a Psyche Analyst-for-Sun-formula trade
scenes.text_anchor: “It's the potion formula to Sequence 4 of the Sun pathway, Unshadowed.”

scenes.setting: News exchange, first topic: Alger profiles the four Pirate Kings and seven Admirals for Justice — the hundred-year-old oldest pirate alive, Admiral of Stars Cattleya estranged from Queen Mystery, and the newcomer who took Qilangos's crew and ship and renamed herself Rear Admiral Ailment
scenes.text_anchor: Admiral of Stars Cattleya was once a follower of Queen Mystery

scenes.setting: Audrey switches topics to the eleven Backlund serial murders, and Derrick — who knows such rituals from the City of Silver's records — identifies them as a Devil's advancement ceremony of the Abyss pathway, thirteen victims minimum and forty-nine at most
scenes.text_anchor: “The Abyss pathway's Sequence 6 is called Devil.

scenes.setting: The serial killer set aside, Audrey asks why so few sell potion formulas at Beyonder gatherings — Alger explains the cost, the loss-of-control risk without the acting method, and the trust a formula sale demands
scenes.text_anchor: “Mr. Hanged Man, there's something that I've been wondering about.

scenes.setting: Audrey suggests sealing the deal with an oath, and Alger names the problem: no one swears in an underground gathering by one of the seven orthodox gods — which turns the table to the statue The Sun found in the Forsaken Land of the Gods, and to Mr. Fool's own naming of it
scenes.text_anchor: “That's the Fallen Creator.”

scenes.setting: Gathering's close: Alger names the True Creator's pathways — and Derrick goes cold, realizing Elder Lovia of the six-member council is a Shepherd of an evil god; Mr. Fool adjourns
scenes.text_anchor: Shepherd? The silent Derrick sat up straight, his eyes filled with horror.

scenes.setting: Alone above the fog, Klein studies Lanevus's badge: spirituality reveals 'January 4, 1350, 8 p.m. in Babur Valley' — a mystic rendezvous beacon, shelved unless Faceless arrives by year's end; then thoughts on how a Magician should act
scenes.text_anchor: “January 4, 1350, 8 p.m. in Babur Valley.”

scenes.setting: A St. George's Borough spare apartment: Fors patches her hair loss while sheltering Xio, who counts her Sheriff-fund earnings and swears off both Audrey's missions and the golden-masked man — mostly
scenes.text_anchor: “I don't want to take on any more of Miss Audrey's missions again!”

scenes.setting: Count Hall's villa: Alfred's telegram — the Rainbow Salamanders have reached Pritz Harbor, bound for the suburb manor; Susie's gift is almost here. 'Woof?'
scenes.text_anchor: “Susie, the gift I prepared for you is almost here.”

scenes.setting: Bell-ringing test laps on the finished bicycle behind Leppard's house: design notes, cost targets, patent plans, second payment — and word of next week's Emperor Roselle Memorial Exhibition at the Royal Museum
scenes.text_anchor: Klein circled the lawn behind Leppard's house a few times on the bicycle

scenes.setting: The volcanic island meet on the Sonia Sea: pirates flee then swoon as Rear Admiral Ailment Tracy docks the Black Death; Admiral of Stars Cattleya walks a starlight bridge from her sailboat — her celestial globe oddly like the glass bottle Alger once owned
scenes.text_anchor: Black Death… Alger whispered.

scenes.setting: Audrey's suburb manor: the 'gift' arrives — two three-meter color-shifting Rainbow Salamanders; mistress and dog wear the exact same stunned expression
scenes.text_anchor: It was a giant lizard whose skin changed color depending on how the light hit it.

scenes.setting: The manor study: Audrey plays it cool over her three-meter 'animal specimens' — then learns Susie completely digested the Spectator potion months ago, unprompted. 'I'm just a dog. Woof.'
scenes.text_anchor: “Susie, have you completely digested the potion?”

scenes.setting: Above the gray fog: Alger sacrifices the Panther spinal fluid and Elf-spring crystals; midweek Derrick's Mist Treant root and juice follow — every Magician ingredient gathered
scenes.text_anchor: “… I've already gathered the Dark Patterned Black Panther Spinal Fluid

scenes.setting: The kitchen brew and the dark living room: fireworks swirl in the bottle, 'Hornacis… Flegrea…' whispers through the pain, one arm ancient and one transparent — until it all settles. Klein stands up a Mid-Sequence Beyonder: a Magician
scenes.text_anchor: At that moment, he was already a Magician.

scenes.setting: Inventorying the Magician: Damage Transfer, Flaming Jump, Air Bullets, Paper Figurine Substitutes, Illusion Creation and more — then the sky clears and the moon swells blood-red days early: the Blood Moon, when the spirit world runs strong
scenes.text_anchor: The most important one was, Damage Transfer!

scenes.setting: A Cherwood apartment under the Blood Moon: the full-moon ravings hit Fors worse than ever — nails snapping, hair growing wild, gods unanswering — until she crawls to the paper with the ancient Hermes name: 'The Fool that doesn't belong to this era… save me, save me…'
scenes.text_anchor: “Save me, save me…”

scenes.setting: Above the fog (visions only: Fors writhing amid overturned furniture): a non-member's agonized prayer arrives; the ravings threading it carry no malice — so Klein extends his spirituality to pull the supplicant in
scenes.text_anchor: at the end of the ancient, mottled bronze table, by the side of The Fool's seat was a clear radiance rippling out

scenes.setting: Fors wakes above the gray fog: her chair's symbol blooms into endless doors (Mr. Door's ravings, Klein realizes); 'that's because you're too weak' — the fix is raising her life's natural order; invited to Monday gatherings, she cuts the deck and draws The Magician
scenes.text_anchor: “The Magician!”

scenes.setting: Fors wakes on her living-room floor under the blood-red disk, alive, un-lost, hair grown long — hugging her knees over a life now completely changed
scenes.text_anchor: I'm not dead, I didn't lose control…

scenes.setting: Above the fog: the layered-door symbol on Fors's chair sets Klein wondering whether the full-moon ravings are Mr. Door's — a mystery for higher Sequences to solve
scenes.text_anchor: Klein looked at the chair which had the symbol of a layered door on its back.

scenes.setting: Dawn at the St. George apartment: Fors deflects Xio's worry with bluster — 'it doesn't affect me at all. Toast a piece of bread for me too!'
scenes.text_anchor: “But it doesn't affect me at all.

scenes.setting: Morning papers scream of the Killer Demon's true 11th murder on Blood Moon night; the Ernst ad signals tomorrow's gathering, plans are laid, and three crude paper figurines get cut for the new Magician
scenes.text_anchor: “Night of the Bloody Moon, the Killer Demon strikes again!”

scenes.setting: A sweating jewelry magnate at the door: Rogo Colloman hires Klein for ten pounds to guard his son Adol — who fell in with lunatics and swears they want him dead — until tomorrow afternoon
scenes.text_anchor: “I'm Rogo Colloman, a jewelry businessman.”

scenes.setting: The gilded Colloman mansion on Grimm Garden Street: shivering Adol's aura is stained wraith blackish-green; Klein meets fellow detectives Kaslana, Lydia and Stuart — and pranks them flat with a mimicked gunshot
scenes.text_anchor: “Protect me, protect me… They're going to kill me! They want to kill me!”

scenes.setting: After a hearty dry dinner: Stuart privately diagnoses Adol as haunted rather than hunted and muses about calling the Lord of Storms' priests — in a couple of days, maybe
scenes.text_anchor: “He looks more like he has a mental problem, or, according to the countryside, he's been haunted by ghosts

scenes.setting: One a.m. watch: corpse-pale Adol drifts to the washroom; Klein follows, tosses Azik's whistle to bait the thing out, snaps his fingers — flame ignites an invisible figure, and Adol wakes from his long nightmare. 'What happened to you?'
scenes.text_anchor: With a loud bang, a flame rose from the ground, igniting an invisible figure.

scenes.setting: The washroom debrief: awakened Adol remembers nothing since the last 'Spirit Dance' — his death-worshipping society digs up corpses for resurrection rituals outside Grimm Cemetery, Fridays at three a.m.; he wants nothing more to do with it
scenes.text_anchor: “They conduct a resurrection ritual outside Grimm Cemetery every Friday at three in the morning.”

scenes.setting: A 'cigarette break' on the balcony: the first Paper Figurine Substitute unfolds into a smoking wax-faced Klein, and the real Magician slips down past the patrolling guards
scenes.text_anchor: Klein violently shook his wrist, causing the paper to make a crisp sound.

scenes.setting: Treetop view of the Grimm Cemetery clearing: eight robed youths whirl a Spirit Dance around a corpse while the tattooed Numinous Episcopate leader proclaims Death's return — and hurls a furious black cat over the body
scenes.text_anchor: “Death! “Honorable Death! “Is about to return!”

scenes.setting: The 'resurrection' works — then goes wrong: the corpse sits up, mauls a boy's neck, ignores Kapusky Reid's whistle-commands 'in the name of Death', and sprints into the forest
scenes.text_anchor: “I command you to return in the name of Death!”

scenes.setting: In the trees, Klein reels the corpse in with Azik's whistle and dead matchsticks: Air Bullets stagger it, snapped-finger flames melt it like a candle, and a Flaming Jump dodges its final claw
scenes.text_anchor: Klein kept snapping his fingers, causing red flames to appear on the ground

scenes.setting: An illusion-painted clown steps from the woods: the fled ringleader is named — ancient-Feysac teacher Kapusky Reid — the youths are sworn to silence on pain of death, and the 'gatekeeper of hell' vanishes into conjured mist
scenes.text_anchor: “I'm just a gatekeeper of hell.”

scenes.setting: Back over the fence, the rusty-marked paper double dismissed, a quiet watch till daybreak: Adol wakes cured, Rogo pledges 300 pounds to the Church, and Kaslana's suspicious questions meet a perfectly cut steak
scenes.text_anchor: “Does Adol waking up and going to the washroom count?”

scenes.setting: Assignment over with a 50% bonus from generous Rogo: fifteen pounds for a night's exorcism, and sober math about the 3000-pound road to Sequence 6
scenes.text_anchor: Rogo Colloman was quite generous in the settlement of his pay

scenes.setting: A half-empty gathering (the manhunt keeps Beyonders home): the marrow crystal goes to the Apothecary for 298 pounds, sedatives, and a clue — Bishop Utravsky at the Harvest Church; Stray Dog's plea to rescue his imprisoned physician friend meets only heavy silence
scenes.text_anchor: “On the south side of the Bridge, on Rose Street, at the Harvest Church, find Bishop Utravsky.

scenes.setting: Not homeward: a change of clothes in East Borough, then toward the border of North and Hillston Boroughs — where Kapusky Reid lives
scenes.text_anchor: It was where the suspected member of the Numinous Episcopate, Kapusky Reid, lived.

scenes.setting: Aulka Street: a hazy-faced intruder interrogates the pigeon-chested teacher — not Numinous Episcopate, not even a Beyonder, just a noob taught the Dance of Death by a dying vagabond who left a copper whistle that summons a three-eyed skull messenger Kapusky can't even see
scenes.text_anchor: “He was a vagabond. He fainted in front of my house because of a serious illness.

scenes.setting: The withered back garden: Kapusky exhumes his teacher's grave — no corpse, no bones, only white feathers dyed in yellow oil
scenes.text_anchor: The bottom layer was littered with white feathers, dyed in yellow oil!

scenes.setting: Over the feather-filled grave: thoughts of angels and Azik's coffin dream; Klein pockets three feathers and confiscates the copper whistle from the terrified teacher, extracting Spirit Dance lore before slipping away
scenes.text_anchor: “Don't blow that copper whistle again.”

scenes.setting: Above the gray fog (visions only: the white-haired, red-spotted corpse tearing feather-winged out of its grave and walking into the darkness): divination brands Kapusky's whistle dangerous to use — for now
scenes.text_anchor: White feathers sprouted from the back of the corpse…

scenes.setting: Empress Borough woods at dawn: the Apothecary — actually a Sequence 8 Beast Tamer, it turns out — ponders how a Beast Tamer acts, locks eyes with a certain large golden retriever, and Susie bolts
scenes.text_anchor: “Then, will my Sequence 7 be able to tame and use humans?

scenes.setting: The piano room: Susie reports meeting her 'natural enemy' with scary eyes; Audrey grounds her from the woods and laments the serial killings canceling tonight's gathering
scenes.text_anchor: “I feel that he is my natural enemy!”

scenes.setting: Saturday breakfast of childhood-style flatbread interrupted: Isengard Stanton proposes a partnership — hunt the serial killer together for the police's 2000-pound reward
scenes.text_anchor: “The police has already offered a reward of 2,000 pounds.”

scenes.setting: The doorstep negotiation and shared carriage: wary of Nighthawks, Klein signs on as analysis-only consultant to Isengard's detective posse — noting the older man's suspiciously warm palm along the way
scenes.text_anchor: “I can participate in the discussion and help to look through the information and analyze the clues

scenes.setting: The detective exchange in Isengard's activity room — sixteen investigators, familiar faces Stuart and Kaslana among them: Klein's one contribution reframes the hunt — pull every unsolved serial murder of the last twenty years; the killer is no rookie
scenes.text_anchor: “I want information on the unsolved serial murders in the last twenty years

scenes.setting: Evening by the fireplace with the delivered dossiers: only nine unsolved serial cases in twenty years — two stand out: the five murdered single mothers of four years ago, and the dismemberments of eleven years back
scenes.text_anchor: There were a total of four in Backlund, five in the other cities, a total of nine in total!

scenes.setting: The little Harvest Church on Rose Street: 2.2-meter Bishop Utravsky of Mother Earth — ex-Feysac pirate turned gentle Father — hears the disguised visitor ask about the Apothecary-formula task and answers with closed eyes: 'Kill me.'
scenes.text_anchor: “My request is…” … “Kill me.”

scenes.setting: 'Kill the old me': the Dawn Paladin's split past self must die at the bottom of his dreamland via a dragon-relic candle — five minutes or vegetate; a quick fog divination says tolerable risk, and Klein preps matchsticks and paper figurines before lighting the human-skin candle
scenes.text_anchor: “I have already reached Sequence 6 of my Beyonder pathway, becoming a Dawn Paladin.”

scenes.setting: Into the mind-world: a ferocious 'Utravsky' falls dead in a staged battle — 'What a professional performance. But I know that this is a dream within a dream.'
scenes.text_anchor: But I know that this is a dream within a dream.

scenes.setting: The duel at the dream's floor: the past Utravsky's Dawn Armor, giant rapier and Hurricane of Light versus a prepared Magician — Flaming Jumps between pre-thrown matches, a paper shield, a decoy matchbox, and finger-snap Air Bullets that crack the unarmored skull; the old warrior dies in scarlet flame
scenes.text_anchor: “I've never said that snapping my fingers could only be used to control flames and not shoot out Air Bullets.

scenes.setting: Back in the real cathedral, Utravsky weeps like a newborn: reward time — Klein passes on the blood-syringe relic and takes the Master Key (opens locks and unreal passageways; side effect: getting randomly lost, promptly demonstrated) plus the Apothecary formula
scenes.text_anchor: “I want the Master Key.”

scenes.setting: Sunday morning: a letter posted to Isengard about the four-year-old case, then the dressed-up Sammers share the news — Mary made the Pollution Council, chaired by Sir Ders Shaw with Hibbert Hall as First Secretary
scenes.text_anchor: “The Chairman of the council is Sir Ders Shaw and the First Secretary is Mr. Hibbert Hall.”

scenes.setting: The Sammers depart for Mary's celebration; Isengard's letter crosses Klein's in the mail with the same shortlist — including the cremated boy suspect — and Klein posts surveillance instructions to Detective Stuart
scenes.text_anchor: Great detective minds think alike…

scenes.setting: Count Hall lectures Hibbert on how councils breed influence — 'only money is multi-faceted' — while a bored Susie relays every word to Audrey, who still can't steer high society toward East Borough's misery
scenes.text_anchor: “Then pretend that you can handle it.

scenes.setting: Monday, three o'clock above the fog: the Tarot Club convenes with a new star — Fors, awed and under-confident, takes her seat as Audrey greets Mr. Fool and eyes the newcomer: 'This is?'
scenes.text_anchor: The Magician had her own illusory star as well.

scenes.setting: Miss Magician's first gathering: mutual profiling all around, Audrey nearly placing Fors by her voice alone, and The Sun asking for information he then realizes he requested before Mr. Fool agreed to it
scenes.text_anchor: “This is Miss Magician, our new member.”

scenes.setting: The World trades what he knows of the True Creator to The Sun — twisted, fallen, mad — and Derrick reads the goatskin again and again, because the creator of everything going mad is the only answer that fits what happened to the City of Silver
scenes.text_anchor: the True Creator was known as the creator of everything!

scenes.setting: The World collects his half of the bargain: the full run-down on Devils — the danger-sensing revenge instinct, animals that can become them too — and the near-impregnable Guardian
scenes.text_anchor: “It's time for you to answer my question,”

scenes.setting: Fors's decoy shopping (Apothecary plus Trickmaster) fools everyone except the Telepathist who knows her; The World sells the Apothecary formula for a 230-pound sacrifice, and Audrey — with Mr. Fool's blessing — sells Miss Magician the acting method itself for a mere 200 pounds
scenes.text_anchor: “The ‘acting method' is a method to speed up the mastery of potions and minimize the risk of losing control.

scenes.setting: Justice teaches Fors the acting method; The Sun buys the Seven Gods from three sellers with answered questions — and his creation myth names the eight ancient gods, among them the King of Demonic Wolves Flegrea: the very word from Klein's advancement ravings, 'the Evernight Demonic Wolf'
scenes.text_anchor: “The King of Demonic Wolves, Flegrea split the remnant powers of authority
